page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 4345P processor featuring 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes a 32 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 123.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, which provides approximately 7.71 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 3890 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core operations, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test scoring 4638.98, placing it in the top 10% of tested servers. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also achieve top-tier status at 50.05 GB/sec and 22.26 GB/sec respectively. The PassMark memory score of 3301.4 is similarly positioned in the top 10%. However, a key hardware tradeoff is observed in memory write bandwidth for large uncached blocks, which is classified as weak at 21.89 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and static web serving throughput fall within the average range.

Given its bare metal architecture and high-capacity local NVMe storage, this server offers high resource density without virtualization overhead. It is suited for database hosting, static web serving, and single-threaded data processing tasks. The inclusion of AVX-512 instruction sets and strong small-model LLM text generation speeds of 414.79 tokens per second also support lightweight machine learning inference workloads.
